name: Multiple Epiphyseal Dysplasia and Pseudoachondroplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for MED and PSACH

criteria.description: Short stature with disproportionate limb shortening and joint pain
Radiographic evidence of delayed and irregular ossification of epiphyses
Identification of pathogenic variants in COMP, MATN3, or related genes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus radiographic epiphyseal abnormalities; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, radiographic, and genetic assessments.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Irregular and delayed ossification of epiphyses
pathognomonic.notes: Key radiographic hallmark differentiating MED and PSACH
searchTerms: uneven or delayed bone growth ends

pathognomonic.symptomName: Disproportionate short stature with limb shortening
searchTerms: short height with short arms and legs

common.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones in early childhood

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb deformities such as genu valgum or varum
searchTerms: mild leg deformities like knock-knees or bowlegs

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord compression due to vertebral abnormalities
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure from vertebra problems
spinal nerve squeezing due to bone issues
growth hormone deficiency causing short height

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing mutations in COMP, MATN3, or related genes
imaging: X-rays showing irregular, delayed ossification of epiphyses
Flattened, fragmented epiphyses with metaphyseal changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COMP gene (most common in PSACH)
Mutations in MATN3 and other genes associated with MED
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical assessment of disproportionate short stature and joint symptoms

redFlags: Progressive joint deformities leading to severe disability
Neurological symptoms suggestive of spinal cord compression
Severe growth retardation beyond typical MED/PSACH presentation
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
Briggs MD, Chapman KL. Pseudoachondroplasia and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia: mutation review, molecular insights and diagnosis. Eur J Hum Genet. 2002.
Orphanet: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia and pseudoachondroplasia. Orphanet Report Series; 2023.
